title: Two-sample comparison through additive tree models for density ratios
abstract: arXiv:2508.03059v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The ratio of two densities provides a direct characterization of their differences. We consider the two-sample comparison problem by estimating this ratio given i.i.d. observations from two distributions. To this end, we propose additive tree models for density ratio estimation along with efficient algorithms using a new loss function, the balancing loss. The loss allows tree-based models to be trained using several algorithms originally designed for supervised learning, such as forward-stagewise optimization and gradient boosting. Moreover, the balancing loss resembles an exponential family kernel, and it can serve as a pseudo-likelihood with conjugate priors. This property enables generalized Bayesian inference on the density ratio using backfitting samplers designed for Bayesian additive regression trees (BART). translated_title: 基于密度比加性树模型的双样本比较
translated_abstract: 两个密度之比直接刻画了它们之间的差异。我们考虑双样本比较问题，即在给定来自两个分布的独立同分布观测数据的条件下估计这一比值。为此，我们提出了用于密度比估计的加性树模型，并借助一种新的损失函数——平衡损失——设计了高效的算法。该损失函数使得基于树的模型能够使用最初为监督学习设计的多种算法进行训练，例如前向分步优化和梯度提升。此外，平衡损失类似于指数族核函数，并可作为具有共轭先验的伪似然函数。这一性质使得能够使用为贝叶斯加性回归树设计的回拟合采样器对密度比进行广义贝叶斯推断。我们的贝叶斯策略为推断出的密度比提供了不确定性量化，这对于应用而言至关重要。
tldr: 本文提出基于新损失函数“平衡损失”的密度比加性树模型，使树模型既能利用监督学习算法高效训练，又能通过广义贝叶斯推断实现不确定性量化，从而完成双样本比较任务。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes additive tree models for density ratio estimation with a new "balancing loss" that enables training via supervised learning algorithms and generalized Bayesian inference with uncertainty quantification, facilitating two-sample comparison.
